# Lightning PM API

Use the authenticated API instead of scraping HTML.

- Base API: `/api/v1`
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` or `X-LPM-API-Key: <api_key>`
- Current user: `GET /api/v1/me`
- List projects: `GET /api/v1/projects` (add `?archive=1` for archived)
- Resolve issue by pasted URL: `GET /api/v1/issues/resolve?url=<issue_url>`
- Load issue by id: `GET /api/v1/issues/{issueId}`
- Read project issue guidelines: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/issue-guidelines` (`descriptionTemplate` — the description skeleton, `guidelines` — the team's issue-writing rules, `naming` — `{requireTitle, requireLabels, example}`); read it before creating an issue and follow it
- Create issue: `POST /api/v1/issues` (name must have a title besides `[label]` prefixes; some projects require at least one label; `priority` is the `1..100` value shown in the UI, default `50`; optional `board`: `true` puts the new issue on the scrum board by its status, a column key puts it in that column)
- Add comment: `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/comments`
- Change an issue in part: `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}` changes only the fields the request carries; today that is `addImages[]` and `addFiles[]`. Answers with the updated issue and notifies its participants, as a web edit does; a request with no supported field answers `400`
- Attach an image or a file (`multipart/form-data`, `POST` only, repeatable field: `-F 'images[]=@/tmp/shot.png'`). Where it lands depends on the field: an **image** (`images[]` at creation, `addImages[]` later) goes to the issue gallery with a preview and a viewer, a **file** (`files[]` / `addFiles[]`) goes to the file list for downloading - a screenshot belongs in the image field, the file field is for when the original file itself is the point. At creation - `POST /api/v1/issues`; to an issue that already exists - `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}`, where both fields add to what is attached; with a comment - `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/comments`, one field `files[]` and no gallery, an image there gets its preview by type anyway (such a comment may go without `text`). Prefer attaching at creation: an attachment added later costs a second request and leaves an edit on a brand-new issue. Limits are the web form's - 10 images and 10 files on an issue, 20 files on a comment, an image at most 10 MB and only jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp, files 128 MB per request and any type - and never send more than 20 attachments in one request, images and files counted together: PHP drops the rest before Lightning PM sees them and says nothing, so 10 images plus 10 files is already the ceiling. A broken limit answers `400` and saves nothing, neither the attachments nor the issue or comment they came with; over the server limit - `413`. Multipart carries every field as a string, so `requestChanges` of a comment and `board` of a new issue take `true`/`false` as strings too
- List project issues: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/issues` (filters: `status`, `type`, `label`, `search`, `limit`, `offset`; `search` looks through the issue name and description, and a plain number also matches that issue number in the project)
- List project labels (tags): `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/labels` (sorted by usage in this project)
- List project members: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/members` (the users who can be assigned to the project's issues; locked users are not listed)
- Read project scrum board: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/board` (issues grouped by columns `todo`, `inProgress`, `testing`, `done`, in board order; each issue carries its `members`, `testers` and `masters`, empty lists when nobody is assigned; `currentSprintNumber` is the sprint the board belongs to; `400` for a non-scrum project)
- Put issue on the board / move between columns: `PUT /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/board` (optional `column` from the same set; without it the column follows the issue status, as the «На доску» button does; `testing` sends the issue to test, `done` completes it)
- Take issue off the board: `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/board` (issue returns to the backlog, status unchanged)
- Close the current sprint: `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/board/close` (required `sprintNumber` — the sprint to close, must be the board's `currentSprintNumber`, any other number is refused with `400` naming the open one, so an accidental repeat closes nothing; optional `transferOpened`, default `false`, keeps the `todo` and `inProgress` issues on the board of the new sprint; the board goes to the sprint archive, issue statuses do not change; answers with the closed sprint, the new sprint number and the lists `archived` and `transferred`; an empty board answers `closed: false` and changes nothing; the action is irreversible; any project member may do it)
- Assign issue participants: `PUT /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/members` replaces the whole set, `POST` adds to it, `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/members/{userId}` takes one off; body `{"users": [id, ...]}`, empty list allowed only for `PUT` and clears the set; `/testers` and `/masters` work the same way; all three are idempotent and answer with the updated issue; an unknown user is rejected with `404`, a locked one or one without access to the project with `400` (never silently dropped)
- List repositories: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/repositories`
- List branches: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/repositories/{repositoryId}/branches`
- Create branch: `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/branches`

Payload conventions, the same everywhere:

- Dates are ISO-8601 and are read back in the shape they are written: a moment in time as `2026-07-15T12:34:56+03:00`, a calendar day without time as `2026-07-15` (that is `completeDate` of an issue, and it round-trips). A date that is not set is `null`.
- A user — issue or comment author, member, tester, master, `GET /api/v1/me` — is always `{id, name, nick, firstName, lastName, avatarUrl, url}`. Issue members carry one extra field `sp`, their share of the issue estimate.

The issue payload reports its board position as `isOnBoard` and `boardColumn` (`null` for an issue in the backlog), and refines `status` with `substatus`: `backlog`, `todo`, `inProgress`, `underTesting`, `passedTest`, or `null` when the status has nothing to refine (in particular for a project without a scrum board).

The issue estimate is `hours`, and `hoursUnit` says what it means: `storyPoints` in a scrum project, `hours` in any other one.

Attachments come in the issue payload as `files` (attached to the issue) and `comments[].files` (attached to a comment), both with the same item shape `{fileId, uid, name, mimeType, size, sizeFormatted, created, url, requiresAuthentication}`. A `url` with `requiresAuthentication: true` needs the same auth header as any other request.

Comments should be high-signal only: use them for tester instructions, caveats, or implementation details not already clear from the issue. Do not post routine progress updates such as branch creation or "implementation started".

An issue URL of this instance written in a description or a comment automatically links the two issues.
